title: Inner product with the zero vector is false
statement: For every $n$-bit Boolean vector $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, the mod-$2$ inner product of $x$ with the all-zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ equals $\mathrm{false}$; that is, $\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} (x_i \wedge 0) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: x is an arbitrary n-bit Boolean input
replaced:
For every $x : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$, the inner product of $x$ with the all-zero
input is \texttt{false}: $\mathrm{innerProduct}(n, x, \mathbf{0}) = \mathtt{false}$.
